title: He must increase (John 3:22–36)
hookLine: the Baptist, happy to fade: he must increase, I must decrease
last: NOT TO CONDEMN BUT TO SAVE.

lines: AENON, BECAUSE THERE WAS MUCH WATER.
cards: A band, a small business, a church plant: anyone who's started one may know the day someone new arrives and the crowds drift over. That's where John the Baptist is now.
He's baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there. Not far away, Jesus is baptizing too. Well, his disciples are; John's Gospel adds later that Jesus himself didn't baptize.
John's followers come to him worried, almost hurt: Rabbi, the one you pointed to across the Jordan, everyone is going to him.

teach.b: John's answer starts with a sentence that would settle a lot of jealousy: "A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven." Whatever you have, you were given.
I told you, he says, I'm not the Christ; I was sent ahead of him. Then a picture from a wedding. The groom is the one with the bride.
The friend of the bridegroom, the best man, isn't jealous. He stands listening for the groom's voice, and when he hears it, he's overjoyed. "This my joy therefore is fulfilled."

teach.h: A GLAD MUST, NOT A SAD ONE.
teach.b: Then the line that names today: "He must increase, but I must decrease." Not a sad must, like talking about getting older. A glad one, like watching a child grow taller than you.

teach.h: JUNE AND DECEMBER: THE LIGHT SHIFTS.
teach.b: His whole work was pointing, and now people are going where he pointed. That's what success looks like for a pointer. Augustine of Hippo, preaching on John the Baptist's feast, noticed something.
The feast of John's birth falls near midsummer, after which the days get shorter. Christmas falls near midwinter, after which they get longer.

teach.h: HE MUST INCREASE, BUT I MUST DECREASE.
teach.b: He must increase; I must decrease, written, Augustine says, into the calendar and the sunlight.
The chapter closes with words, whether the Baptist's or the Gospel writer's, about the one who comes from above: the Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand.

how: Churches in the West and East keep the birth of John the Baptist on June 24, near midsummer in the northern hemisphere, and 'he must increase, but I must decrease' is quoted by some Christians as a motto for humble service.

o: the best man who stands beside the groom at a wedding
Jesus, pictured as the groom his friend serves gladly
a rival teacher who pulled the crowds away from John

games.q: you're John the Baptist. your disciples are upset: everyone is going to the one you pointed to. what do you say?
o: he must increase, but I must decrease.
games.why: "he must increase, but I must decrease." like the best man, he says, "this my joy therefore is fulfilled."

practice: Think of someone whose star is rising near you, a colleague, a sibling, a friend whose project is taking off, someone who might honestly make you a little jealous.
Picture them succeeding, notice whatever you feel without scolding yourself, and try the best man's posture: beside them, listening, glad. If you pray, give thanks for them.

wordCard.voice: Bridegroom, the one the best man serves without envy — John the Baptist's picture for Jesus, as the crowds left him: joy, not rivalry, like hearing the groom's voice.

orig.note: Greek: he must increase, grow. 'dei', must, is the same word as in 3:14: the Son of man must be lifted up.

carryVoice: Your line: this my joy is fulfilled. Joy, not rivalry, like the best man's. Until tomorrow.
